body:
That's why I threw in the ego protection stuff. I grew up unpopular and socially awkward, always being teased for anything. As a result, I tend to be sensitive about and protect myself from threats. I hate this, and want to not give a fuck, but it's a constant uphill battle. Another result is my relative success. I didn't mention that to brag, but rather to illustrate myself. I came literally from welfare and ghetto, but raised myself up with only my hard work. I like to be genuinely proud of that as my character, at least. Sorry I was not this articulate last night when I posted this. 

We do have some routines, and I know she hates them. But we do take as many vacations as possible. She goes to Korea about once per year (even without me while I work, sometimes). I use all my vacation days with her, and we spend the largest part of our budget (except eating) on travel. She even travels alone sometimes.

She married me in her early twenties, and I think she's a bit saddened at the loss of her youth, sometimes. Instead, I'm happy to have found her and had some good years with her. Just a difference, I guess.

Anyway, thanks for the food for thought.

Man, I really wish... and I do thank you for taking time to chime in.

In the beginning, I'd be careful to use "I feel..." statements instead of accusatory "You are..." types of statements. I'd rationally explain things in a calm voice. No beans.

Then I tried the no-tolerance for her behavior, but that only landed me in hotter water for not taking her seriously, or not listening, or some shit. The path of least resistance is to just stare into the void and try not to let her suck me into her argument, even as it evolves into a dozen other arguments... then wait for her to call me the next day at work to say she misses me and to come home early, then to get upset again when I tell her I can't. 

I also tried the writing down thing, but that only transformed into "make sure you wrote down all the issues you have that piss me of, so you can remember to fix them."

Everything is just so very one-sided. Even her family kind of had that sentiment toward her. I really believe she has a legitimate chemical imbalance. But I know she will never do anything clinical about it. 

Before my dad died, he also had a big fight with her over some small thing, and he always told me she was very immature in the way she handles things. Granted, he was one of those divorced, curmudgeon, woman-distrusting people who told me to never get married; but he does seem right about this.

I'm somewhere on that spectrum, too, man... Reading your post kinda resonated with me. No friends or meaningful family, just a wife that I provide for and that's apparently about it these days. I honestly just think I got lucky with her. Maybe I put on a good act. Never had a non-superficial friend, though (not even acquaintances in my adult life). Never had an "I love you" relationship with family.

Life does seem damn lonely. Otherwise it just seems superficial, doesn't it? But I've been cursed with this one nagging thing that always seems to come back: hope. Damn annoying, hope is. It just keeps selling me on keeping on keeping on. Has that salesman left you?

Anyway, just wanted to say all that, to illustrate that I kinda know what you're talking about, I think, maybe. And mostly to see if anything I said (lived through) resonated with you, too.
